# Time and media

> Status: AI-drafted, not human-reviewed

Group id: `time-media`. Observe the page over time and consume its media: time limits, moving and flashing content, autoplaying audio, captions, audio description, sign language and text alternatives. Collection is mostly waiting, recording and extracting; judging needs a person to watch and listen for most media criteria, which is why many outcomes here are `cantTell` for an AI.

## Setup

- Chromium started with autoplay allowed (`--autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required`) so that autoplay is observable, viewport 1280 x 800, a virtual audio sink (for example a PulseAudio null sink) so that audio output can be recorded by a script.
- Tools (open): `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` for frames and stream data; an open speech recogniser such as Whisper for timed transcripts; a photosensitive-epilepsy flash analyser (for example the free PEAT) for flashing; DevTools Protocol `Emulation.setVirtualTimePolicy` or a fake clock to skip long waits.
- A person: headphones, the media player's caption and audio-description controls, a way to pause. Do not look at suspected flashing content without an analyser run first.
- AI: audio and video understanding if available; otherwise only the extracted data (transcript, frames, track list) can be judged.

## Collect

Collect all of this before judging. Each item names the data type (`needs` key in the data file). A script or a cheap model can do it without judgement; store each artifact with a file name that the report can cite.

1. **media** — Inventory of media and moving content: `audio`, `video`, `object`, `embed`, `iframe` (embedded players), `canvas`, SVG animation (`animate`, SMIL), animated GIF/APNG/WebP, CSS `animation` and `transition` with `infinite` or duration over 5 s. Per item: selector, source, `autoplay`, `loop`, `muted`, `controls`, duration, `track` elements (kind, srclang, src), nearby links labelled transcript, audio description, sign language, or text version.
2. **media** — For each media file: download it and run `ffprobe` (duration, audio and video streams, subtitle streams, loudness); extract one frame per second; for flash checks extract every frame at native frame rate. Store a timed transcript from speech recognition and the text of every caption track.
3. **timing** — Page-load audio: load the page with no interaction; for 30 seconds record, once per second, which media elements are playing (`paused === false`) and the RMS level of the recorded audio output; record the time audio stops, whether a visible pause/stop/mute control exists in the first 5 focusable elements, and whether activating it stops the sound.
4. **timing** — Motion: record the top-of-page viewport as screenshots every 500 ms for 20 seconds; compute pixel difference between successive frames; list changing regions with their element selectors (from `MutationObserver` counts per second and running CSS animations via `document.getAnimations()`). For each moving item that runs longer than 5 seconds: look for a pause, stop or hide control, activate it, and record the effect.
5. **timing** — Time limits: search the DOM and scripts for `meta[http-equiv=refresh]`, `setTimeout` or `setInterval` handlers with delays over 20 seconds that navigate, hide or sign out, visible countdowns, and text matching `session|expire|time ?out|minutes|seconds left|inactivity`. Then leave the page idle for the stated time (use virtual time for long waits) and record what happens; record whether a warning, a way to extend (and how many times), and a way to turn the limit off exist.
6. **timing** — Interruptions: during the motion and idle observations, record `alert`/`confirm` dialogs, new windows, overlays, notifications, and content injected without user action, with times; look for a setting that postpones or suppresses them.
7. **interaction** — Animation from interaction: scroll the whole page in 100 px steps and click or hover each interactive element once, with screenshots before and 500 ms after; record motion triggered. Repeat the whole run with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` emulated (`Emulation.setEmulatedMedia`) and compare.
8. **multi-page** — If the page is a step in a process that has a time limit, record the step number, the time-limit text, and whether entered data is preserved after expiry (details in the multi-step-flow recipe).

## Judge

Outcomes on perception of media (captions, description, sign language, background audio, live) need a person who has watched and listened. An AI may produce a candidate list from the extracted data; it reports `cantTell` unless it has verified the media.

### 1.2.1 Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded) (A)

- **Fails when:** Prerecorded audio-only content has no transcript, or prerecorded video-only content has neither a text description nor an audio track presenting the same information (F30, F67 when the alternative does not serve the same purpose).
- **Passes when:** A transcript presents all speech and meaningful sounds; for video-only, a text or audio alternative presents the visual information.
- **Common false positives:** Media that is itself a labelled alternative to text on the page; media with synchronised audio and video (see 1.2.2 and 1.2.3).
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** You cannot verify that the transcript is equivalent.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-and-video-only-prerecorded.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F30, F67 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.2.2 Captions (Prerecorded) (A)

- **Fails when:** Synchronised prerecorded media with speech has no captions, or captions omit dialogue or meaningful sounds (F8, F75), or are out of sync.
- **Passes when:** Captions (open or closed) with dialogue and meaningful non-speech sounds, in sync.
- **Common false positives:** Video without an audio track; media labelled as an alternative to text; subtitles in the same language that contain sound information count as captions.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** No speech recogniser for the language; a track exists but you have not played it.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-prerecorded.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F8, F75, F74 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.2.3 Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (A)

- **Fails when:** Prerecorded video has important visual information that is not in the soundtrack, and neither audio description nor a full text alternative is provided.
- **Passes when:** An audio description track or a text alternative of the whole media exists.
- **Common false positives:** A talking head where all information is spoken; media labelled as an alternative to text.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Decide which visual information is important: an AI lists candidate moments (frames with no matching speech) and reports `cantTell`.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-or-media-alternative-prerecorded.html>

### 1.2.4 Captions (Live) (AA)

- **Fails when:** Live synchronised media with speech has no live captions.
- **Passes when:** Live captions are provided.
- **Common false positives:** No live content on the page: `inapplicable`.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Live content cannot be observed from a page snapshot: `cantTell`.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/captions-live.html>

### 1.2.5 Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AA)

- **Fails when:** Prerecorded synchronised video with important visual information has no audio description (see F113); a text alternative alone is not enough at AA.
- **Passes when:** An audio description track or a description version of the video exists and describes important visuals.
- **Common false positives:** A video where all visual information is spoken.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** The judgement of what is important and whether the description is adequate belongs to a person; an AI reports `cantTell` with its candidate list.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-description-prerecorded.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F113 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.2.6 Sign Language (Prerecorded) (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Prerecorded audio with speech in synchronised media has no sign language interpretation.
- **Passes when:** A sign language track or video is provided.
- **Common false positives:** Media without speech.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Only a sign language user can judge the interpretation; an AI can only record that an interpreter is shown.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/sign-language-prerecorded.html>

### 1.2.7 Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded) (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Where pauses in the soundtrack are too short for description, extended audio description is not provided.
- **Passes when:** Extended audio description is available, or the pauses suffice.
- **Common false positives:** Videos with enough pauses.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Needs a person who watches and judges: `cantTell` for an AI.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/extended-audio-description-prerecorded.html>

### 1.2.8 Media Alternative (Prerecorded) (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Prerecorded synchronised media and video-only content have no text alternative that covers all audio and visual information.
- **Passes when:** A full text alternative (transcript with descriptions) is provided.
- **Common false positives:** Media that is itself an alternative to text.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Completeness cannot be verified without watching.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/media-alternative-prerecorded.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F74 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.2.9 Audio-only (Live) (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Live audio-only content has no text alternative.
- **Passes when:** A live text alternative exists.
- **Common false positives:** No live audio: `inapplicable`.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Live content cannot be inspected from the page: `cantTell`.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-only-live.html>

### 1.4.2 Audio Control (A)

- **Fails when:** Audio that plays automatically for more than 3 seconds without a control at the top of the page to pause or stop it, or to change its volume independently of the system volume (F23, F93).
- **Passes when:** No sound plays automatically, or it is at most 3 seconds, or a working pause, stop or mute control is near the top.
- **Common false positives:** Muted autoplay video; axe `no-autoplay-audio` is incomplete when it cannot read the duration: use the recorded time.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Sound that starts only after a script event you could not trigger.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/audio-control.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F23, F93 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 1.4.7 Low or No Background Audio (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Prerecorded speech audio has background sound louder than 20 dB below the speech, with no way to turn it off.
- **Passes when:** No background sound, or it can be turned off, or it is at least 20 dB lower.
- **Common false positives:** Audio that is not mostly speech; singing and rapping; captcha audio.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Level difference in a mixed track cannot be measured reliably: `cantTell`.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/low-or-no-background-audio.html>

### 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable (A)

- **Fails when:** A time limit with no way to turn it off, adjust it (at least 10 times the default) or extend it (a warning of at least 20 seconds, extend with a simple action at least 10 times): meta refresh (F40, F41) or a server-side redirect after timeout (F58); a script that signs the user out without warning.
- **Passes when:** No time limit, or an exception applies (real-time event, essential, longer than 20 hours), or the user has the controls above.
- **Common false positives:** Animation durations; debounce delays; a countdown for a real auction.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** A server-side limit that you cannot trigger within the waiting time.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F40, F41, F58 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A)

- **Fails when:** Moving, blinking or scrolling content that starts by itself, lasts more than 5 seconds, is shown with other content, and has no pause, stop or hide control (F16); automatically updating content (carousel, ticker) with no control or setting (F50).
- **Passes when:** Motion lasts at most 5 seconds, or can be paused, stopped or hidden, or is essential or part of an activity.
- **Common false positives:** A loading indicator; motion inside a video that has its own controls; very small changes such as a blinking cursor.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** You cannot tell whether a movement is essential.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/pause-stop-hide.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F16, F112, F50, F7 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 2.2.3 No Timing (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Any time limit other than for real-time events or non-interactive synchronised media.
- **Passes when:** There are no time limits.
- **Common false positives:** As 2.2.1 for exceptions.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Server-side limits not observed.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/no-timing.html>

### 2.2.4 Interruptions (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Interruptions (pop-ups, automatic redirects F40, F41, notifications, live updates) cannot be postponed or suppressed by the user, except emergencies.
- **Passes when:** The user can postpone or turn off interruptions.
- **Common false positives:** User-initiated dialogs; emergency messages.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Interruptions that depend on server events you did not see.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/interruptions.html>
- W3C failure techniques for this criterion: F40, F41 (<https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Techniques/failures/>)

### 2.2.6 Timeouts (AAA)

- **Fails when:** A time limit for inactivity that can cause data loss, and the user is not warned of its length.
- **Passes when:** A warning states the duration, or data is kept for at least 20 hours.
- **Common false positives:** Processes with no data entry.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** The duration of an unannounced limit cannot be verified.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timeouts.html>

### 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold (A)

- **Fails when:** More than three flashes in any one second that exceed the general or red flash thresholds in a large enough area. Use the analyser verdict.
- **Passes when:** The analyser reports no failure, or no content flashes more than three times in a second.
- **Common false positives:** Small flashing areas under the area threshold; slow fades.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** Without an analyser run on frame-accurate capture: `cantTell`. A model cannot judge flashes from sparse screenshots.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes-or-below-threshold.html>

### 2.3.2 Three Flashes (AAA)

- **Fails when:** More than three flashes in any one second, of any size (count only).
- **Passes when:** At most three flashes per second.
- **Common false positives:** Fades and gradual transitions.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** As 2.3.1.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/three-flashes.html>

### 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions (AAA)

- **Fails when:** Motion animation triggered by interaction (parallax, scroll-linked movement, large transitions) that cannot be disabled and is not essential.
- **Passes when:** The animation stops or reduces under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, or a setting disables it, or it is essential.
- **Common false positives:** Colour or opacity fades; non-motion transitions.
- **Answer `cantTell` when:** It is unclear whether the motion is essential.
- Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/animation-from-interactions.html>

### 2.2.5 Re-authenticating (AAA)

Also checked in `multi-step-flow`. Here only record time limits and warnings in the step. Understanding: <https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/re-authenticating.html>

## Already covered by tools

Our retest showed that rules detect obsolete `blink`/`marquee` elements, meta refresh and autoplaying media elements with known duration; they cannot judge captions, description, flashes, script timers or CSS and JavaScript animation. HTML_CodeSniffer emits one notice per media element.

- **1.2.1** (partial) axe: audio-caption; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_2_1.G158, 1_2_1.G159,G166. Retest (2 failing cases): axe 1 asked for review, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 notice. Rules only notice that audio or video exists and ask for a check; they cannot judge whether an alternative exists or is equivalent.
- **1.2.2** (partial) axe: video-caption; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_2_2.G87,G93. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 asked for review; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. axe asks for review when a video has no track element; neither tool judges caption accuracy or synchronisation.
- **1.2.3** (partial) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_2_3.G69,G78,G173,G8. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. The 1.2.3 sniff is only in the WCAG2AA ruleset; in WCAG2AAA the related 1.2.5/1.2.8 sniffs give page-level notices. axe has no rule.
- **1.2.4** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_2_4.G9,G87,G93. No test case in the 2026 retest. Only a notice asking for a manual check; live captions cannot be inspected from the page.
- **1.2.5** (partial) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_2_5.G78,G173,G8. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. Notice only, emitted per video; no rule can tell whether an audio description track exists or is adequate.
- **1.2.6** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_2_6.G54,G81. No test case in the 2026 retest. Notice only; no rule can detect sign-language interpretation.
- **1.2.7** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_2_7.G8. No test case in the 2026 retest. Notice only; whether pauses are too short for standard description is a judgement.
- **1.2.8** (partial) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_2_8.G69,G159. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. Notice only, emitted per video; no rule checks for a full text alternative.
- **1.2.9** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_2_9.G150,G151,G157. No test case in the 2026 retest. Notice only; live audio cannot be inspected from the page.
- **1.4.2** (partial) axe: no-autoplay-audio; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_4_2.F23. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 asked for review; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 notice. axe checks autoplaying media elements and asks for review when duration is unknown; HTML_CodeSniffer only gives a notice. Audio started by script is missed.
- **1.4.7** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 1_4_7.G56. No test case in the 2026 retest. Notice only; background level in mixed audio cannot be measured by page rules.
- **2.2.1** (partial) axe: meta-refresh; HTML_CodeSniffer: 2_2_1.F40.2, 2_2_1.F41.2. Retest (3 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 missed; WCAG2AA supplement 2 flagged, 1 missed. Rules catch meta refresh only; script timers and session timeouts are missed. The 2.2.1 sniff is missing from the WCAG2AAA ruleset; the WCAG2AA supplement (D-024) catches the meta refresh cases.
- **2.2.2** (partial) axe: blink, marquee; HTML_CodeSniffer: 2_2_2.F4, 2_2_2.F47, 2_2_2.SCR33,SCR22,G187,G152,G186,G191. Retest (4 failing cases): axe 1 flagged, 3 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 4 missed. Rules catch obsolete blink and marquee only; CSS/JS animation and auto-updating content are missed.
- **2.2.3** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 2_2_3.G5. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only.
- **2.2.4** (partial) axe: meta-refresh-no-exceptions; HTML_CodeSniffer: 2_2_4.SCR14. Retest (3 failing cases): axe 2 flagged, 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 3 missed; WCAG2AA supplement 2 flagged, 1 missed. Rules catch meta refresh only; script interruptions such as pop-ups and live updates are missed.
- **2.2.6** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: no sniff. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. No rule; data-loss timeouts are server behaviour.
- **2.3.1** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: no sniff. Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. Neither tool analyses flashing. Dedicated flash analysers (outside our toolset) can decide this from video frames.
- **2.3.2** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 2_3_2.G19. Retest (2 failing cases): axe 2 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 2 missed. Notice only; see 2.3.1.
- **2.3.3** (none) axe: no rule; HTML_CodeSniffer: 2_3_3.C39. Retest (1 failing case): axe 1 missed; HTML_CodeSniffer WCAG2AAA 1 missed. Notice only.

## AI and human

Taken from the data file (`ai.level`, `human.level`). Levels: AI likely/possible/unlikely; human must/should/optional.

- **1.2.1** Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded): AI possible (needs dom, media); human should. AI: A model can transcribe audio and describe video, then compare with the alternative, but equivalence errors are easy to miss. Human: Equivalence of the alternative to the media needs a person who has watched or listened to it.
- **1.2.2** Captions (Prerecorded): AI possible (needs dom, media, timing); human should. AI: Speech recognition can compare captions with the dialogue; non-speech sounds and timing are error-prone. Human: Caption accuracy, completeness and sync need a person to confirm.
- **1.2.3** Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded): AI unlikely (needs media, timing); human must. AI: Deciding which visual information is important and whether the soundtrack or a text alternative conveys it needs reliable video understanding. Human: A person must watch the video and judge whether the important visual information is available.
- **1.2.4** Captions (Live): AI unlikely (needs media, timing); human must. AI: Live events are hard to capture for analysis and captions depend on what happens live. Human: Needs a person observing a live stream.
- **1.2.5** Audio Description (Prerecorded): AI unlikely (needs media, timing); human must. AI: Judging whether description covers the important visual information needs reliable video understanding. Human: A person must watch with audio description and judge adequacy.
- **1.2.6** Sign Language (Prerecorded): AI unlikely (needs media); human must. AI: A model may notice that an interpreter is shown, but cannot verify the interpretation. Human: Only a sign-language user can judge the interpretation.
- **1.2.7** Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded): AI unlikely (needs media, timing); human must. AI: Requires judging whether standard description would be insufficient. Human: A person must watch and judge.
- **1.2.8** Media Alternative (Prerecorded): AI possible (needs dom, media); human should. AI: A model can compare a transcript with transcribed audio and described video, but completeness is error-prone. Human: Completeness of the text alternative needs confirmation.
- **1.2.9** Audio-only (Live): AI unlikely (needs media, timing); human must. AI: Live content cannot be captured reliably for analysis. Human: Needs a person observing the live audio.
- **1.4.2** Audio Control: AI likely (needs dom, media, timing); human optional. AI: Detecting audio playing for more than 3 seconds and a control near the top is observable in a scripted browser. Human: Scripted observation settles it.
- **1.4.7** Low or No Background Audio: AI unlikely (needs media); human must. AI: Separating speech from background in a mixed track and judging 20 dB is not reliable. Human: A person must listen.
- **2.2.1** Timing Adjustable: AI possible (needs timing, interaction, dom); human should. AI: Waiting and observing can reveal limits; long or server-side limits are hard to trigger. Human: Confirm the limit and the adjust/extend options.
- **2.2.2** Pause, Stop, Hide: AI possible (needs timing, screenshot, interaction); human should. AI: Screenshots over time show motion; finding and testing pause controls is error-prone. Human: Confirm pause/stop/hide works.
- **2.2.3** No Timing: AI possible (needs timing, interaction); human should. AI: Same limits as 2.2.1, without exceptions. Human: Confirm.
- **2.2.4** Interruptions: AI possible (needs timing, interaction); human should. AI: Observing a page over time reveals interruptions; whether they can be postponed needs interaction. Human: Confirm.
- **2.2.6** Timeouts: AI possible (needs multi-page, timing, dom); human should. AI: Can read warnings in the flow; verifying actual timeout duration is slow. Human: Confirm.
- **2.3.1** Three Flashes or Below Threshold: AI possible (needs media, timing); human should. AI: Only with frame-accurate capture fed to a flash analyser; models cannot judge flashes from sparse screenshots. Human: Use a flash analyser rather than human viewing, which is risky; a person confirms the result.
- **2.3.2** Three Flashes: AI possible (needs media, timing); human should. AI: Same as 2.3.1; the count rule (no more than three) is simpler than the threshold. Human: Same as 2.3.1.
- **2.3.3** Animation from Interactions: AI possible (needs interaction, timing, screenshot); human should. AI: Comparing behaviour with and without prefers-reduced-motion emulation finds some cases. Human: Whether motion is essential is a judgement.

## Report

Write one finding per criterion and location. Use exactly these fields.

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `criterion` | Success criterion id, for example `1.4.3` |
| `outcome` | `failed`, `passed`, `inapplicable` or `cantTell` |
| `location` | Page URL plus CSS selector of the element (or `page` for page-level findings) |
| `evidence` | One to three sentences of fact: what was observed, with numbers where they exist. Name the collected artifact (file name or step number in the trace) |
| `confidence` | `high`, `medium` or `low` |
| `tester` | `human` or the model id of the AI that judged |

Rules:
- `failed` needs evidence that shows the failure; do not write it from a guess.
- `passed` means that this tester checked the criterion across the collected data and found no failure; it is not a conformance claim.
- `inapplicable` means the content the criterion is about does not exist on the page (state which content you looked for).
- `cantTell` means the data cannot decide it. Say what is missing and which pass or person could decide.
- One finding per element and criterion; do not merge different locations.

Example (JSON, one finding):

```json
{"criterion": "2.4.7", "outcome": "failed", "location": "https://example.org/form#nav a.skip", "evidence": "No visible change between focused and blurred crops at focus step 3 (focus-trace/step-03.png): outline is none, no replacement style.", "confidence": "medium", "tester": "claude-sonnet-5-5"}
```
